clue.text: Cloistered away, hiding name that is embarrassing

indicators.note: the convent phrase hides the other letters, keeping them inside itself

parts.note: someone cloistered away is shut up in a convent, so the phrase gives IN CONVENT
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is' (id est)

explanation.surface: Someone shut away in a cloister keeps quiet about a name, which is awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: The inner letters go in as IE then N, just before the final T of the convent phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something embarrassing is awkward or troublesome to deal with.

clue.text: Storms into lead from inspired run, with game points

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its opening letter, so this takes the start of 'inspired'

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
RU is rugby union, the game
PTS is the usual abbreviation for points

explanation.surface: A sports report: an inspired run plus points lets a team storm into the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storms into' looks like part of the sports report but is the definition; RU (rugby union) is a common crossword game.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to burst or rush violently into a place is to storm into it.

clue.text: Wanting to know scoundrel's keeping promise

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a cur is a scoundrel; the possessive adds the S
an IOU is a written promise to pay

explanation.surface: Someone eager to learn whether a rogue will honour his word.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's on 'scoundrel's' counts as a letter here, and 'keeping' signals that the promise sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a curious person is inquisitive, eager to find things out.

clue.text: Myself and I, when in Rome

definitions.meaning: the Roman numeral I stands for the figure one

explanation.surface: A play on 'me, myself and I' and 'when in Rome, do as the Romans do'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: number one is slang for oneself, and Roman I is the first number.

clue.text: Sexy? It's bold to strip off for acclaim

indicators.note: stripping off removes the outer layer, so each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Is undressing a sexy, bold act that earns praise?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to strip off' removes both ends of each word: sEXy, iTs, bOLd.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to praise someone highly or hail them is to acclaim them.

clue.text: Pouring shot for cliquey set

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or wrecked, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A snobbish crowd sharing drinks being poured.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an exclusive circle of insiders is a clique.

clue.text: Time in the city, year off to make business contacts

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
off means taken away, removing a letter

parts.note: New York is often just called the city

explanation.surface: Spending time in town, with a year off, to meet useful business people.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to network is to cultivate professional connections.

clue.text: National fervour to interrupt heartless neoconservative ramble

indicators.note: taking the heart out of a word leaves only its two end letters
interrupting means breaking into, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to ramble is to wander
zeal is fervour

explanation.surface: Political passion breaking into a rambling neocon speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' is a noun here: a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen; a Kiwi citizen is one example, hence a definition by example.

clue.text: Cockney's picked up booze and amplifier

parts.note: a Cockney drops the H of 'heard', a synonym for picked up
rum is a kind of booze

explanation.surface: An East Londoner has collected some drink and a sound system.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously drop their H's, so 'heard' becomes 'EARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The membrane in the ear magnifies sound vibrations, a playful description rather than a dictionary one.

clue.text: Golfer welcomes hit leaving one closer

indicators.note: welcoming takes something in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Tiger Woods is the golfer

indicators.note: leaving means a letter departs from the word

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A golfer taking a shot that ends up nearer the hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something tighter is more closely packed or nearer together.

clue.text: Manage to catch Ed Balls admitting current employment problems

indicators.note: catching means holding something inside, so ED goes within

parts.note: to run something is to manage it
taken as written

indicators.note: admitting lets something in, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: balls are formal dances
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Politician Ed Balls is caught up in jobs trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls is a former Labour shadow chancellor, a British politician; his name splits into two pieces here.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay-offs, jobs cut when no longer needed, are a classic problem in employment.

clue.text: Love 100 lines that's part of Gettysburg address?

parts.note: zip means nothing, like love in tennis
C is the Roman numeral for 100
an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: Lincoln's short Gettysburg speech, about 100 lines, delivered with love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' is a postal address, not Lincoln's speech; Gettysburg is a town in Pennsylvania with its own US postal code.
explanation.definitionFit: A US postal number is part of any mailing address, including one in Gettysburg.

clue.text: Emperor's house with entrance to palace past it

parts.note: Leo is one of the astrological houses of the zodiac

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its opening letter

parts.note: someone past it is old

explanation.surface: An emperor's residence, where the palace entrance is getting decrepit.
explanation.definitionFit: Name: several Holy Roman rulers, such as Leopold I, bore this name.

clue.text: Family members back in part of church

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: sis and pa are a sister and a father
pa is a father

explanation.surface: Relatives returning to sit in a part of their church.
explanation.definitionFit: Variant term: an apsis is an apse, the vaulted recess at a church's east end.

clue.text: Frank has wrong number around radius

indicators.note: around means placed on both sides of another piece

parts.note: out means wrong, as in 'your sums are out'
N is the mathematical abbreviation for a number
a spoke is a radius of a wheel

explanation.surface: A man named Frank dialled a wrong number from somewhere nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone frank speaks their mind bluntly.

clue.text: Money is English pound, perhaps

parts.note: legal tender is money

explanation.surface: Money is the English pound, by way of example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' is not sterling but a verb: beating meat to soften it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: pounding steak is one way to soften meat; 'perhaps' marks it as one method.

clue.text: Feature of Oxford: quiet dons in the morning, working alone

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the quiet letters wear the morning letters around them

parts.note: a.m. means in the morning
sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: working letters are being reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Oxford lecturers keep quiet early in the day, working alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like Oxford academics but is the verb 'puts on'. The anagram of ALONE gives OLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashmolean is Oxford University's famous museum of art and archaeology, a landmark of the city.

clue.text: "Yes" to reform adopted by ugly place, a small state

indicators.note: being adopted means being taken in by the other piece

parts.note: a hole is a dump, an ugly place

indicators.note: reforming reshapes, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ugly little statelet adopts a policy of saying yes to reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges the quoted word, and 'adopted by' sets the result within a dump-like ugly place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican's papal see is a tiny sovereign state.

clue.text: Old Turk's twist on Islam

indicators.note: a twist distorts, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Ottoman giving his own spin to Islam.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names an Ottoman Turk, from Osman, founder of the dynasty.

clue.text: Power remains with American governor

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: An American governor's power and what is left of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic title: a pasha was an Ottoman provincial governor.

clue.text: Dangerous, mean and almost rotten

parts.note: par is the average or mean

indicators.note: almost means one letter short, so the last is dropped

parts.note: lousy means rotten

explanation.surface: Something risky that is also nasty and nearly decayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a parlous state is perilous, full of danger.

clue.text: Park behind road's end in city, after one's reversed

indicators.note: after means the city piece follows the turned letters
reversed means the two letters swap round

parts.note: one is I, and 's stands for 'is', giving I and S

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the city word

parts.note: a city is a large town

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Directions for parking in town, behind the end of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Park behind' is not about leaving a car: it means 'park your behind', i.e. take a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful idiom: parking your backside on a chair means taking a seat.

clue.text: Not a call girl's problem

indicators.note: not means leaving the letter out

parts.note: to dial is to call on the phone
taken as written, the letter removed
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A predicament not faced by a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call girl' is not a prostitute: 'call' is DIAL and 'girl' is EMMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dilemma is a difficult choice, a problem.

clue.text: Boatman may have you thus puzzled

definitions.meaning: a boatman may take you out onto the ocean

explanation.surface: A boatman leaves you puzzled.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being lost on the ocean figuratively means being confused or baffled.

clue.text: Boy inhaling grass is unpredictable

indicators.note: inhaling takes something in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name
to grass is to inform, and a rat is an informer

explanation.surface: A lad smoking cannabis behaves erratically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' suggests cannabis but is the informer sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: erratic behaviour is irregular, hard to predict.

clue.text: Objects to exhibit, dropping first and second

indicators.note: dropping the first means its opening letter goes

parts.note: to present is to show or exhibit

explanation.surface: Someone objects to an exhibition that loses first and second place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first and second' looks like one phrase but splits: 'dropping first' deletes, 'second' adds S.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to resent something is to take offence at it, to object.

clue.text: I really drink hard, needing elementary variety

parts.note: so means really, as in 'so good'
to tope is to drink heavily

explanation.surface: A confession of heavy drinking needing basic variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elementary' means of a chemical element, not basic.
explanation.definitionFit: Example sense: one form of a chemical element, differing in neutron count, is a variety of it.

clue.text: Shop where sales enticed swarms

indicators.note: swarms suggests a milling crowd, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A food shop where tempting sales draw in crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a deli is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and fine foods.
